The recipe builds and installs static FFTW into the build prefix, but the packaged FFmpeg configuration does not enable libfftw3 and disables librubberband; FFTW is not incorporated into or shipped with the package.
The GPL-2.0-or-later source notice belongs to build-only FFTW; the packaged FFmpeg configuration omits libfftw3 and disables its librubberband consumer.
The disabled documentation repeats FFTW's GPL-2.0-or-later and commercial-license explanation; neither the documentation nor FFTW code is shipped in the package.
The recipe statically builds FriBidi and enables libfribidi in packaged FFmpeg; source headers grant LGPL-2.1-or-later and the exact pinned COPYING file is packaged.

The recipe builds a static libsamplerate in the build prefix, but packaged FFmpeg has no libsamplerate option and disables librubberband; the library is not incorporated into or shipped with the package.
The documentation explains the 2016 relicensing to BSD-2-Clause, but documentation and build-only libsamplerate code are absent from the distributed package.
The recipe statically builds dav1d and enables libdav1d in packaged FFmpeg; the exact BSD-2-Clause file is packaged for binary redistribution.

TwoLAME's source headers license the library under LGPL 2.1 or any later version; the package carries the exact COPYING bytes from the pinned revision because FFmpeg's LGPLv3 license file is not a substitute.
The default GME build compiles gme/ext/emu2413.c into libgme, so its exact MIT notice is packaged.
The GPLv2 MAME YM2612 implementation is an unselected alternative; the recipe leaves GME_YM2612_EMU at its LGPL Nuked default.
The static libgme selected by the recipe is linked into packaged FFmpeg; the exact LGPL text is packaged and corresponding-source obligations remain a release gate.
The recipe statically builds GMP and packaged FFmpeg enables it; SPLICR selects GMP's LGPL-3.0-or-later option and retains its exact terms.
GMP also offers a GPL-2.0-or-later alternative; the distribution selects LGPL-3.0-or-later but preserves this exact upstream alternative-license text for completeness.
LGPLv3 incorporates GPLv3 terms; the exact GPLv3 text accompanying this pinned GMP source is therefore packaged with the LGPL supplement.
The recipe builds static libkvazaar and packaged FFmpeg enables libkvazaar; its exact BSD notice is packaged without claiming codec patent clearance.
Greatest is referenced only by Automake check_PROGRAMS tests; the recipe runs make and make install, not make check, so it is absent from libkvazaar and the package.
The selected Autotools build lists src/threadwrapper only under EXTRA_DIST and does not compile it into libkvazaar.
The upstream additional licensing information requires preservation and explicitly grants no patent license; the exact text is packaged without asserting patent clearance.
The Clear BSD LCEVCdec core is statically incorporated because packaged FFmpeg enables liblcevc-dec; the exact license is packaged.
LCEVCdec adds its utility and FFmpeg-libs dependency only for executables or tests; both are disabled by the recipe.
The BtbN recipe invokes CMake directly with its cross-toolchain and does not execute the repository's Conan packaging recipes.
The target is win64 with the BtbN MinGW toolchain, so the Emscripten toolchain and wrapper path are not used.
fmt is required only by LCEVCdec utility/sample targets; the recipe disables executables and tests, so that subtree is not added.
Gradle belongs to non-Windows wrapper/build tooling and is not invoked by the direct CMake/Ninja win64 recipe.
The target is win64 and uses the BtbN MinGW toolchain, not the bundled iOS CMake toolchain.
JSON configuration defaults off and the only nlohmann_json consumer is the utility subtree, which is excluded because executables and tests are off.
Vulkan Memory Allocator is referenced only by the Vulkan pipeline; the recipe explicitly sets VN_SDK_PIPELINE_VULKAN=OFF.

nalloc is included only by the example fuzzer sources; examples are explicitly disabled and the code is absent from libvpx.a.
